name: ACCORDION
description: Accordion is a single-player patience game where all cards are laid into one row and compressed into piles by matching suit or rank. A card can move onto the pile immediately to its left or three positions to its left. The goal is to finish with one pile.

content.text: Accordion is a single-player patience game where all cards are laid into one row and compressed into piles by matching suit or rank. A card can move onto the pile immediately to its left or three positions to its left. The goal is to finish with one pile.

Rules for The Idle Year published by William Brisbane Dick (1883) and Tarbart (1905). Wood & Goddard (1940) recorded it as Tower of Babel. The name Accordion appears in the 1950s (Culbertson, Goren). Parlett equates Accordion with Idle Year, Methuselah and Tower of Babel.
One player. Accordion is a patience (solitaire) game played by a single player; there are no opponents or partners.
One shuffled deck and table space for a long row of piles.
Deal cards one by one from stock into a single row. After each deal, resolve any legal compression moves before dealing again if playing the incremental style.

items.text: Deal-All First: Deal all cards to the row first, then start moving.
Play-As-You-Go: Deal one card at a time; resolve moves before dealing next. Original style, exceedingly difficult.
Queen and Her Lad: Jones 1892. Q♥ as commencing card, J♥ at bottom of stock. Discard cards between two of same suit/rank.
Royal Marriage: Reduce deck to King and Queen of same suit, placed at start and end of layout.
Nidgi Novgorod: 1904 Standard Hoyle. Two equal-rank cards at top/bottom of pack; deal 4 in row; discard inner cards when outer match.
